payload.title: Todos with due dates and an overdue view

work_items.title: Optional due date on todos, overdue flag on every todo, and GET /todos/overdue
work_items.intent: Let people see when a task is late without breaking any current client. The intent has five parts. (1) A client may send an optional due date when it creates a todo. A request with only a title behaves exactly as today. (2) Every todo the API returns carries its due date (null when unset) and a boolean `overdue` flag. The flag is true only when the todo is not done and its due date has passed. A todo with no due date is never overdue. This applies to GET /todos, the new overdue list, the POST /todos response and the POST /todos/{id}/complete response. (3) GET /todos/overdue returns exactly the overdue todos, in the same order as GET /todos (ascending id). It returns an empty list when nothing is overdue. (4) A malformed due date is rejected with 422, in the same way an empty title is rejected today. (5) The existing three tests in tests/test_todos.py pass without edits. New API tests in tests/ prove each rule above, including the boundary of the due date itself and the case of a completed todo whose due date is in the past. The README and the endpoint list in the app/main.py docstring mention the new field and endpoint.
work_items.notes: Shared names (proposed, the spec can confirm): request field `due_date` (optional, default null); response keys `due_date` (ISO-8601 string or null) and `overdue` (bool); route `GET /todos/overdue`. Facts from research: a todo today is a stdlib dataclass serialised by `asdict` in `Todo.to_dict()` (app/storage.py:10-17), with keys id, title, done, created_at. Routes return plain dicts and have no response_model (app/main.py:25-46). `TodoIn` has only `title` and no extra='forbid' (app/main.py:16-17). There is no GET /todos/{todo_id} route, so a literal GET /todos/overdue cannot be shadowed. If someone adds such a route later, it must be registered after /todos/overdue. The only clock is `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` called directly in a default_factory (app/storage.py:15), and there is no injectable clock. Pitfalls to avoid: (a) `overdue` must be computed when the response is built. If it is stored at creation it goes stale. (b) Tests that depend on 'now' must be deterministic. Use due dates far in the past or future, or a clock the tests can control. Tests must not sleep. (c) No test compares a whole todo dict today, so adding keys is safe. The existing assertions on id == 1, done, created_at and `== []` must keep holding. (d) No new dependency: parse dates with stdlib datetime or pydantic's built-in date/datetime types. Platform: no change to service_manifest.json (no new env vars, migrations stay `true`), and .github/workflows/preview.yml deploys the branch unchanged.

payload.summary:
This outcome is one small, coherent change to a 100-line FastAPI service, so it is one work item that becomes one pull request. A todo gets an optional due date when it is created. Every todo the API returns gets a computed `overdue` flag. A new `GET /todos/overdue` endpoint returns the open todos whose due date has passed. Existing clients that send only a title get exactly the fields they get today, with the same values. The two new keys appear alongside them: `due_date` set to null and `overdue` set to false.

I considered splitting the work in two (the due-date field and flag first, then the overdue endpoint) and decided against it. Both parts depend on one rule for what 'overdue' means, and a reviewer has to approve that rule once, together with the tests that pin it down. Separately each part would be tiny (XS), and the split would only add a merge dependency. The tests and the README note go inside the same item, not into separate items.

The item is flagged for owner judgement for one reason: what counts as 'past due' is a product decision. The choices are whether the due date is a calendar date or a date-and-time, which timezone is used, and whether a task becomes overdue on its due date or only after it. Proposed defaults are listed under open questions. Nothing here needs a database, a new dependency, a new environment variable or a change to the service manifest. The existing preview workflow deploys it as it is.

payload.comments: Approved by Claude on the owner's instruction to run the pipeline through to a pull request. Use the defaults for the open questions: calendar dates (YYYY-MM-DD), overdue applies to open todos only, past due dates are accepted, due_date is present as null when unset.

payload.summary:
Pass, with no blocking issues, but two owner decisions are needed before a full run. There is one spec for the one work item. The round-1 blocker is fixed: AC-10 (a todo due today turns overdue the next day, untouched) is now user-visible, and its internal rules are a separate AC-11. All 13 round-1 issues were addressed, though the import-scan fix is itself defective. Strong: the overdue rule is exact (open, due before today's UTC date). Dates are validated strictly; on pydantic 2.14, the prescribed check rejected all 12 AC-9 values with 422. Fixed signatures make every response read the clock once. Scope is five files, and tests/test_todos.py must stay byte-identical. Both metrics map to tests in tests/.

Decide at Gate 2:
(1) Preview checks cannot pass yet. The deploy step in preview.yml is a placeholder, although the decomposition says the workflow deploys the change as it is (SET-01, upstream, unchanged since round 1). Wire a real deploy, or accept pytest plus the local e2e runs (OQ2).
(2) AC-10 cannot be observed on a preview in one run. rollover-verify exits 3 on the seed day, which the e2e contract counts as a failure. OQ3's default ('exit 3 is not a failure') would make the check vacuous, and it assumes the acceptance OQ2 refuses to assume. Do not take that default as written (ISS-14).
(3) Confirm the rule that a todo is overdue only once its due date is before today's UTC date (OQ1). The spec cites Gate 1 notes in human_comments.md, which I was not given.

Contested: S2=1, because AC-11(c)'s fake clock, read literally, fails a correct implementation (ISS-15). S12=1 (ISS-14). S10=1: 197 lines but 28 KB, with repetition. Command 5's import check rejects the standard library's unittest.mock and itertools and lets requests and time_machine through (ISS-16).

Read first: AC-10, AC-11, the rollover e2e entries, and OQ2 and OQ3. The platform-contract skill was unavailable, so S11 was judged against the manifest schema; the manifest is valid.

payload.comments:
Decisions from the owner, recorded by Claude on the owner's instruction to run this pipeline through to a pull request.
(1) Preview environment: the orchestrator runs every `target: preview` entry against an instance of the service it starts itself from service_manifest.json (entrypoint, health path) on a free port, and exports that as $BASE_URL. Treat that as the preview environment; keep the preview entries that can pass against a freshly started instance.
(2) AC-10 (the overdue flag flips when the UTC date passes): remove the two preview rollover entries (seed / verify). No single-run check against a live instance can observe a date rollover, and a non-zero exit from rollover-verify would be counted as a failed check. The clock-patched pytest tests plus the `rollover-local` entry (which drives the clock in-process) are the authoritative evidence for AC-10; say so in AC-10's verification and keep AC-10 user_visible.
(3) Confirmed rule: a todo is overdue iff it is open and its due_date is strictly before the current UTC calendar date. Calendar dates only (YYYY-MM-DD), past due dates are accepted on create, and due_date is present as null when unset.
(4) Fix the import-scan command the judge called defective so it exits 0 on an implementation that only imports the allowed modules.

payload.summary:
Result: pass. 0 blocking, 2 major, no criterion at 0. One spec covers the one work item. Both round-1 blockers are fixed. The MD is now a rendering of the JSON: every JSON string appears in it, and only the e2e commands are abbreviated. AC-10 follows round-1 option (a).
Read first: three decisions cite human_comments.md (1)-(3). That file is in none of my inputs and not in the spec's produced_by.inputs. Confirm each one. (1) says the orchestrator starts the service from the manifest and exports $BASE_URL. The repo says otherwise: preview.yml:4 'The orchestrator never deploys', the Deploy step is an echo placeholder (preview.yml:64-73), and the README says to replace it. If (1) is wrong, none of the 9 preview e2e entries can run, and the evidence is pytest plus local-all and rollover-local. (2) is the AC-10 waiver: no preview rollover check. (3) is the rule: open AND due_date < today's UTC date.
Verified: I built the change in a scratch clone as the interfaces describe it. All 11 test_plan commands exit 0 (29 tests; base 6dec694 has 3). With fastapi 0.143 / pydantic 2.14, the str+pattern+validator design returns 422 for all 16 AC-9 values. A plain date field would accept '2026-11-30T00:00:00' and 0.
Strong: one exact rule, typed interfaces, five-file scope, exhaustive malformed-input list, local e2e that fails on wrong builds.
Scores below 3: S2=1 (AC-11's Given names the base commit). S12=1: the AC-7 and AC-10 preview entries cannot fail on the defect they cover, though both are honestly labelled and have local counterparts. S8, S10 and S11 are 2. All others are 3.
Minor: the planned pytest tests always patch today_utc, so a date.today() build passes all of them. AC-1's preview check cannot assert id 1. 'listing' does not say whether the rule is checked on every element.
Not verified: the platform-contract skill was unavailable (/mnt/skills is empty). S11 was judged from the rubric, the manifest (valid) and its schema.

payload.comments: Approved by Claude on the owner's instruction. The three decisions the judge asked to confirm stand: (1) the orchestrator starts the service from service_manifest.json on a free port and runs every target=preview entry against it as $BASE_URL; (2) AC-10 is evidenced by the clock-patched pytest tests and rollover-local, no preview rollover check; (3) overdue iff open and due_date strictly before the current UTC calendar date.
